examples.knowledge_point: Calculating the Area of the Parallelogram Spanned by Two Parallel Vectors
examples.problem: Calculate the area of the parallelogram spanned by $\textbf{u}=\langle 3,-2 \rangle$ and $\textbf{v}=\langle 6, -4 \rangle.$
examples.worked_solution:
First, we construct a matrix where the columns are made up of the components of the corresponding vectors:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14043024/assets/b25d71fb75afcb5e4f9e8ce137ec69fb1dfda54aa544b1636e11503273527844.png)

Then, we find the determinant:

$$
\begin{aligned}det(M) & =|\begin{aligned}3 & 6 \\ -2 & -4\end{aligned}| \\  & =3\cdot (-4)-6\cdot (-2) \\  & =0\end{aligned}
$$

The absolute value of $\det(M)$ gives the area $A$ of the parallelogram:

$$
A = |\,0\,| = 0
$$

Calculate the area of the parallelogram in the figure.
feedback.worked_solution:
From the diagram, we get the vectors

$$
\text{u}=⟨3,2⟩,\,\text{v}=⟨2,-2⟩.
$$

First, we construct a matrix where the columns are made up of the components of the corresponding vectors:

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}3 & 2 \\ 2 & -2\end{aligned}]
$$

Then, we find the determinant:

$$
\begin{aligned}det(M) & =|\begin{aligned}3 & 2 \\ 2 & -2\end{aligned}| \\  & =3\cdot (-2)-2\cdot 2 \\  & =-10\end{aligned}
$$

The absolute value of $det(M)$ gives the area $A$ of the parallelogram:

$$
A=|-10\,|=10
$$
